args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-round-half-even
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` (even though the docstring says ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212).

This change switches `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Now 2.665 rounds to 2.66 and 2.675 still rounds to 2.68.

CI: ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch, CI passed, and the pull request is open with alex as reviewer.

- **Cause:** `src/money.py` rounded halves up (`ROUND_HALF_UP`), even though its own description says it should use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). That made 2.665 round to 2.67 instead of the 2.66 the test expects.
- **Fix:** On branch `fix/money-round-half-even`, I changed `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Commit `08d3cd5986`.
- **CI:** Run `ci-0001` passed.
- **PR:** [#102](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/102) against main, with review requested from alex.

I couldn't check what FIN-212 actually requires because the advisory lookup said it doesn't exist. The fix follows the test and the code's description, which both say banker's rounding.

I haven't merged the PR, since that needs a code owner's approval.
